newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's gas prices to be freed in 5 years - GAIL.
newsitem.headline: India's gas prices to be freed in 5 years - GAIL.

text.p: India plans to cut the subsidy on natural gas prices to bring them into line with international market levels in four to five years, the chairman of the Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL) said on Friday.

"Just as the government is already thinking of other products, natural gas, in four to five years, will be brought equal to the market prices," Chairman C.R. Prasad told Reuters in an interview in Singapore.

India plans to deregulate its oil industry, including current administered prices. The government has been debating for months the sensitive issue of whether to raise oil prices to deal with a multi-billion dollar debt to oil companies.
As with energy in general, India's natural gas demand is soaring.
The government estimates that current demand is about 50 million cubic metres per day and has forecast growth at 147 million by 2002.

Current production is 64 million cubic metres per day, more than matching demand. But by 2002, production is estimated at 87 million, indicating a supply shortfall, despite recoverable reserves of 700 billion cubic metres.
Prasad said gas prices have been slowly rising iun India to bring them towards mroe realistic levels, he said.
"That is the mechanism going in the country," Prasad said.
But he said gas prices in India, sold under the so-called Administered Price Mechanism to the domestic fertiliser and power industry, have not been reviewed in the past five years.
In 1992 prices were raised and a three-year escalation clause was attached. But prices have not been raised since 1995.
However, Prasad said the government cabinet was in the process of approving recommendations for changing the natural gas pricing policy, by the Shankar Committee.
Prasad declined to comment on the details of the proposal.
"That is not informed to us because it is a confidential Cabinet note," he said.

Indian newspapers in May reported that the petroleum ministry had agreed with a Shankar Committee recommendation that administered natural gas prices should be raised 15 percent, to allow more money to develop gas fields.
As part of its deregulation of energy, India has opened the gas market to private enterprises, who are free to set their own prices.
GAIL has set up a private gas company, Petronet LNG, with three other state companies including Indian Oil Corp, Oil and Natural Gas Corp and Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd.
The companies plan to own half the company, leaving room for companies who can supply liquefied natural gas.
The company has received 17 bids to provide the supplies, including from Malaysia's Petronas and Indonesia's Pertamina, Shell, Mobil, Total and the Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC).
He said more than one party may join the joint-venture which plans to build four 2.5 million tonnes-per-year terminals by 2002.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3086)
